focus: Core JavaScript fundamentals, framework-specific questions (usually React in the Pakistani market), and a practical UI round - often live coding a small component rather than an abstract algorithm problem.
topics: JavaScript fundamentals - closures, the event loop, prototypal inheritance
React - hooks, reconciliation/rendering, state management
CSS layout - flexbox/grid, responsive design
Browser performance - the rendering pipeline, lazy loading, bundle size
Accessibility basics - semantic HTML, ARIA roles
note: Many interviews build a small real component live (a debounced search box, a todo list) instead of a LeetCode-style puzzle - practice building things quickly under a timer, not just solving algorithms.

focus: API design, data modeling, and the fundamentals behind how a server handles load - usually a mix of conceptual questions and a hands-on design or coding task.
topics: REST API design - status codes, versioning, pagination
Database design - normalization, indexing, transactions
Authentication/authorization basics - JWT, OAuth flows
Caching strategies - Redis, CDN, HTTP cache headers
Concurrency and async request handling
note: Expect to be asked why you made a design choice, not just what the choice was - e.g. why you indexed a particular column, or chose a queue over a direct call.

focus: Breadth across the whole stack rather than deep specialization in one layer - interviewers probe how you reason about where logic belongs.
topics: Client-server data flow and API contracts
State management - client-side vs. server-side, and when to use each
Basic database design alongside UI/UX tradeoffs
Authentication across the full stack (session/token handling end to end)
Deployment basics - how your code actually reaches production
note: A common question style is 'where would you put this logic - client or server, and why?' - be ready to justify tradeoffs across layers, not just describe each layer in isolation.

focus: Platform lifecycle, UI state management, and increasingly - given how many Pakistani teams ship cross-platform - comfort with Flutter or React Native alongside native fundamentals.
topics: Activity/Fragment or ViewController lifecycle
State management - native (ViewModel/LiveData, Combine) or cross-platform (Provider/Bloc, Redux)
Offline-first design - local storage, sync strategies
Native vs. cross-platform tradeoffs (performance, platform API access)
App performance - memory leaks, frame drops, startup time
note: Many Pakistani mobile roles are actually Flutter or React Native roles, not pure native - check the job post's stack before assuming you'll be quizzed on Swift or Kotlin specifically.

focus: CI/CD pipelines, containerization, and cloud fundamentals - often with a scenario question about diagnosing an outage or scaling an existing system.
topics: CI/CD pipelines - build/test/deploy stages, rollback strategies
Containers - Docker fundamentals, basic Kubernetes concepts
Infrastructure as code - Terraform/CloudFormation basics
Monitoring and logging - what to alert on, how to debug from logs alone
Core cloud concepts - networking, load balancing, auto-scaling (AWS/Azure/GCP, whichever the team uses)
note: Scenario questions are common - e.g. 'a deploy just broke prod, walk me through how you'd find and fix it' - practice narrating a debugging process out loud, not just naming tools.

focus: A mix of applied statistics, data manipulation in Python, and practical model-evaluation judgment - most Pakistani roles in this category are applied/ML-engineering, not pure research.
topics: Python data tooling - pandas/numpy fundamentals
SQL for analysis - aggregations, window functions
Model evaluation - precision/recall, overfitting, train/test/validation splits
Core ML concepts - supervised vs. unsupervised, common algorithm tradeoffs
Data pipeline basics - cleaning, feature engineering, handling missing data
note: Most roles tagged "AI/ML" in the local market are applied-engineering positions (integrating or fine-tuning existing models) rather than research positions - expect practical data-handling questions more than theory-heavy ones.

focus: Manual testing fundamentals first, then automation tooling - a strong grasp of how to design a test case matters more than knowing every tool.
topics: SDLC/STLC and the bug lifecycle
Test case design - equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis
Automation tools - Selenium/Playwright/Cypress fundamentals
API testing - status codes, payload validation, tools like Postman
Basic SQL for data verification
note: Interviewers often hand you a vague feature ("test this login form") and want to see how many edge cases you think of, not just whether you know a tool - practice narrating your test-case thinking out loud.
